english.title: Use transplantable material from body of living person - Human Tissue Act 2004
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) used for the purpose of transplantation transplantable material, namely **(..SPECIFY THE MATERIAL..), which had come from the body of a living person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), and when you did so you knew or might reasonably have been expected to know that the material had come from the body of a living person
english.legislation: Contrary to section 33(2) and (6) of the Human Tissue Act 2004.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 33(3)-(5) of the Human Tissue Act 2004 provides exceptions to the offence and a defence where a person believes that an exception applies.
(ii) Section 33(7) of the Act provides that reward has the same meaning as in section 32 and transplantable material means material of a description specified by regulations made by the Secretary of State.

other.penalty:
Fifty one weeks imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the penalty is six months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
